rationale: This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race scores this design with no later chance to correct it. Iteration 10 is the best raced design (931.57). It finished 20/20 on all three development tracks (oval 937.6, s-bend 931.5, slalom 925.7), with rms_error 0.009 to 0.012 and max_error 0.02 to 0.023, well inside the 0.06 m off-track limit. Earlier changes that were tested and reverted (base_speed 0.95, kd 0.45 with 1.1 speed, kp 3.5, and a 1.2 speed to save time) gave no reliable gain. The remaining score levers are small: about 15 points for line-loss events (currently about 1.0 per run) and about 4 points for every 0.2 s of completion time. Each of those changes risks off-track exits on an unseen shape, which costs 500 points per run. So I am keeping the iteration 10 design unchanged, since its completion margin is the most reliable evidence available. Hypotheses to check from this race: the sensor lead at y=0.08 keeps the slalom and s-bend completing on the held-back-style bends, and line_loss_events stay near 1 per run, which suggests a small future gain from kd or a sensor-lead change but no change is justified now. Expected result: completion on all tracks with a score near 930. Failure signs: any off-track exit on an unseen track would point to the sensor lead being at its limit, with y=0.075 the fallback.
